keyFindings.description: The remedy written in place of the false cause cannot be executed as written. The paragraph tells an operator to delete the stale /legion/scratch/<role> directories of roles that are not running, and a plain rm -rf cannot: the go command writes the module cache read-only, mode 555 on every extracted module directory, so rm exits 1 and leaves bytes behind. I reproduced it myself rather than taking the tester's number — one 391 KB module downloaded into a scratch GOMODCACHE, then the delete the sentence names: 31 Permission denied lines, exit 1, 83 KB of the 391 KB surviving, and chmod -R u+w first makes it exit 0 and remove cleanly. One detail my run adds that the scale measurement does not show: what survives is the extracted module source, while the re-downloadable cache/download goes, so the partial delete removes the cheap half and keeps the expensive one. The tester measured the same failure on the real volume at scale: 11,393 denied lines, exit 1, 147 MB left. Every per-role directory of the intermediate layout holds such a cache — that is what the 14 GiB was — so an operator who follows the sentence gets a partial reclaim and an error to diagnose, in the one paragraph of this change that has now been corrected twice. One clause closes it, and half a sentence is worth adding beside it: rm exits 1, so a scripted remedy fails loudly rather than silently, which is the one mercy in the current shape.

I checked the document rather than the diff summary, and the sentence pair that contradicted each other at :1220 and :1233 no longer does.

ciShapes: The default check-runs page is 30 and these commits carry 25 to 39; read with per_page=100 and --paginate or required names fall off it.
A push that carries code and handoff together leaves the code commit with no run of its own; the head that merges is the one GitHub judged.

A required workflow can have many runs on one head, because pr-title fires on every pull-request edit; the newest decides, and a run cancelled because a later one superseded it leaves no verdict rather than a red one.
While a pull request is CONFLICTING, GitHub runs no `on: pull_request` workflow for any of its activity.
The non-required `dispatch` and `dispatch-memory` lanes have rarely settled on this branch.
